title: 6. Epoch mismatch and revocation race
summary: Reunion occurs across an epoch boundary while a revocation races a still-coherent acceptance path. Connectivity returns, but truth does not rewind.
difference_from_quorum_lab: The critical question here is not ceremony admission. It is what a reunited system should do when fresh revocation collides with slightly older acceptance.
notes: This scenario teaches that newer revocation can dominate while still leaving a visible race scar.
Recontact does not erase the earlier acceptance history.
expected_merge_tensions: Island B still carries a coherent acceptance for Iona at epoch 83.
Island A receives a stronger revocation at epoch 84 just before reunion.

initial.policy_summary: Fresh admissible evidence dominates stale, trust weight and corroboration quality dominate raw count, and material conflict survives as residue.

iona.explanation: Iona is stable before the revocation arrives.
Iona remains coherent on Island B.

events.label: Island B keeps Iona accepted
events.description: Island B does not yet see the revocation and continues with a coherent acceptance path.

island_b.log: Island B continues to treat Iona as accepted at epoch 83.

events.label: Island A receives a newer revocation for Iona
events.description: The revocation lands one epoch later with stronger admissible evidence.

iona.explanation: Revocation arrives with newer, stronger evidence.

island_a.log: Island A removes Iona after the revocation lands in epoch 84.
